nodes.label: Fitness-Fatigue (Banister) Model
nodes.rationale: Used as the derivation of calendar rules and penalty geometry, never as a live per-athlete simulator: Bayesian cross-validation (Sci Rep 2025) shows the FFM is ill-conditioned, fitness/fatigue parameters are poorly identifiable, and the fatigue term adds no predictive ability. Constraints k1<k2, tau1>tau2 formalize that fatigue is larger but shorter-lived than fitness.

nodes.label: Busso Variable Dose-Response Model
nodes.rationale: Chosen over plain Banister because the linear model cannot generate a taper endogenously (its optimum is train infinitely hard). Making the fatigue gain a state variable with memory (tau3 ~2.3 d) produces the inverted-U and an optimal daily training load, which is what makes a taper pay off. Consequence: a taper only improves performance if pre-taper training exceeded ODT. The report re-implemented this model and reproduced Thomas & Busso 2005 within 1 pp and 2 days.

nodes.label: Tau-2 Fatigue Decay Constant
nodes.rationale: The single free parameter the whole spread of published peaking recommendations collapses to: every taper event is a fixed multiple of tau2. App default 12 d, clamp [8,18], derived from bodyweight, training age, age, equipment, weight cut, and arrival fatigue; surfaced to coaches as a named fatigue-clearance profile, never a raw number, because per-athlete fitting is indefensible.

nodes.label: Tau-1 Fitness Decay Constant
nodes.rationale: Fixed at 30 d (Issurin's 30 +/- 5 d maximal-strength residual; Busso's fitted 30.8 d), never exposed as a dial because it is statistically unidentifiable from performance data (Hellard tau-correlation 0.99). Its sole use is capping realization-block length at ~28-30 days: a block longer than the strength residual is training you cannot express.

nodes.label: Taper Duration Law (d_opt ~ 1.6 x tau2)
nodes.rationale: From the validated simulation grid: taper duration is almost entirely a function of tau2 (ratio 1.52-1.75 in every non-degenerate cell) while tau1 sets how deep the volume cut can go. Coach-chosen cut form: d_opt ~ tau2 x (2.6 - 0.018 x cut%).

nodes.label: Asymmetric Peak Penalty (0.19/0.10 delta-squared)
nodes.rationale: The peak is flat and asymmetric: a taper too short costs ~2x per day what too long costs (loss% = 0.19 delta^2 short vs 0.10 delta^2 long), and +/-3 days is essentially free, so the UI must not imply day-level precision. When uncertain, taper longer - but never extend complete cessation, which is a separate hard clock.

nodes.label: Overreach Taper Law
nodes.rationale: A planned overreach week demands a deeper AND longer taper: add ~5-8 days and ~8-12 percentage points of volume cut, capped at 28 d / 70%. The direction is robust (Williams 2017 bench +6.4%, Travis 2021 total +7-10%) even though the cycling-calibrated tau3 under-represents resistance-training residuals.

nodes.label: Three-Stage Taper (T1/T2/T3)
nodes.rationale: Resolves the apparent contradiction between Pritchard's 7-10 day survey taper and Travis's 3-week trial taper as a definitional artefact: the survey measures the final step down, the trials measure the whole reduced-load window. T1 onset -30%, T2 deep taper -50% at 90-92.5% intensity, T3 meet week -70-75% with primers, averaging ~50% cut over ~20 days.

nodes.label: 7-Day Training Cessation Ceiling
nodes.rationale: The app's only truly hard constraint: complete cessation of 2-7 days maintains or improves strength, but >7 days costs 1-4% of maximal strength outright and >=14 days shows measured decrements. Encoded as a blocking validation, not a soft warning, because it swamps every soft timing error.

nodes.label: Deadlift Taper Asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Step taper gave DL +1% vs +8% exponential - the deadlift wants a longer, gentler reduction. Acute lab recovery is equal across the three lifts (Belcher 2019), so per-lift offsets (DL:SQ:BP last-heavy 1.00:0.82:0.55, cessation 5.8/4.1/3.9 d) are kept but labeled practice-derived, not a claim that deadlift muscle damage lasts longer; the once-weekly DL concentrates weekly load into one session higher on the fatigue curve.

nodes.label: Peak Projection Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Snap ideal day-offsets to real training sessions furthest-out first, then repair ordering invariants. Tie-breaks differ by lift on purpose: earlier for SQ/DL (too-short is the steeper 0.19 delta^2 branch) and later for BP (shortest fatigue residual, highest technical-decay risk). Taper start snaps forward only - never start the cut early; 5-day splits must actively delete meet-week sessions past cessation.

nodes.label: Peak-Quality Score
nodes.rationale: Split into a soft continuous component (penalty geometry per event, weighted per lift, converted to expected kg) and hard-rule deductions, because a 12-day cessation costs whole percent of 1RM while timing errors cost fractions. Grades A-D; UI shows the grade, per-lift delta timeline, and the single highest-value fix. The current engine audits at roughly grade B/C: 92% ceiling leaves the second attempt unvalidated and meet-week primers are 15-20 pp too light.

nodes.label: Short-Runway Triage (3-6 wk)
nodes.rationale: The strength you have is the strength you will express: over 3-6 weeks the training block adds ~1-2% while the taper adds +3.2-4.4%, so the taper is worth 2-4x the block and is cut last. Cut order: accumulation -> accessories -> variation breadth -> frequency above 2/3/1 -> deloads -> overreach -> never the taper. Realization is always ~3 weeks absolute, not a percentage of prep length.

nodes.label: Arrival Fatigue Input
nodes.rationale: The single input that should reshape a short prep: fatigued arrival means tau2 +2 and an all-taper prep; fresh/undertrained arrival means tau2 -1, train harder for longer and taper less, because a taper from below the tolerance ceiling costs performance (Thomas & Busso). Most apps get this backwards by treating the taper as a fixed share of prep length.

nodes.label: Day-Offset Table (Taper Event Calendar)
nodes.rationale: Every taper event as offset = clamp(round(coef x tau2), lo, hi): taper start 1.70, top calibration single 1.50, last heavy DL 0.92, SQ 0.75, BP 0.50, last touches 0.48/0.34/0.33. At tau2=12 it reproduces every published source (Pritchard, Grgic, Travis, JTS, Rob Palmer) - validated line by line.

nodes.label: Optimal Daily Training (ODT)
nodes.rationale: The inverted-U optimum daily load beyond which more training makes steady-state performance worse - the model-side statement of the MRV concept, produced by the Busso model's fatigue-gain memory.

nodes.label: Travis et al. 2021 (Step vs Exponential Taper)
Belcher et al. 2019 (SQ/BP/DL Recovery Time Course)
Linear Intra-Block Ramp (Factory Scheme)
nodes.rationale: Factory default lerp(startPct, endPct, t): predictable, auditable, one arithmetic pipeline from training max to attempts, best for novices and realization-into-taper. Honest critique: monotony/accommodation, fatigue masking fitness at the highest percentages, %s anchored to a stale 1RM, junk-volume entry weeks, and no volume progression. Meta-analyses find no significant linear-vs-undulating difference, so alternatives are equal-citizen tools, not upgrades.

nodes.label: Wave Loading Scheme
nodes.rationale: 3-week micro-ramps (reps 5/4/3, DL 4/3/2) whose drop-backs shed fatigue while slower-decaying fitness is retained - a built-in mini-deload every third week without stopping progress. Final wave pinned to factory ceilings (SQ 79/82.5/86, BP 78/81.5/85, DL 80/83.5/87) so realization and attempt math chain unchanged; each earlier wave -2.5% per step; N not divisible by 3 truncates wave 1 from the front so the block always ends on the full top wave. Evidence framing: fatigue-management structure with strong practitioner consensus, not proven superior.

nodes.label: Daily Undulating Periodization (DUP) Scheme
nodes.rationale: Because the app's split is lift-per-day, honest DUP is a hybrid of three mechanisms: across-week undulation for 2-slot lifts (bench; squat on 5-day), within-day zone pairing (DL strength + RDL hypertrophy), and week-parity rotation for 1-slot lifts. Zones H 4x8 @ 65-71, P 4x3 @ 68-72 bar-speed, S 4x5 @ 75-81 (S-DL 4x4 @ 76-82), ordered H->P->S per Zourdos. UI framing: comparable to linear in trials; advantage cases are trained lifters and bench - never better.

nodes.label: Hypertrophy Off-Season Scheme
nodes.rationale: Volume-first 8-12 week block with no meet: main-lift variations (load modifiers scale weights) on a 4x12 @ 60-63 -> 4x10 @ 64-68 -> 4x8 @ 70-72 meso spine, secondaries 3x8 at main-2, accessory volume doubled, factory deload week reused verbatim every ~5th week. Bands deliberately capped because 12s above ~63% or 10s above ~68% blow past RPE 8 on the engine's own table; 1RM must be re-tested before %-based strength work resumes. Ships as a decode-safe additive StartPhase.hypertrophy.

nodes.label: HPS Zone Order
nodes.rationale: Hypertrophy -> power -> strength ordering of each lift's weekly exposures, chosen because Zourdos 2016 showed HPS beat HSP in competitive powerlifters (greater squat/bench volume and bench 1RM gains).

nodes.label: Harries et al. 2015 (LP vs UP Strength Meta-analysis)
Grgic et al. 2017 (LP vs DUP Hypertrophy)
Stronger by Science: Periodization Data Review
Powerlifting Coaching Skill (SKILL.md)
nodes.rationale: Reference-grade doctrine written to ~/.claude/skills/powerlifting/SKILL.md so future sessions advise around the frozen engine instead of re-deriving it: block doctrine, RPE/e1RM, FFM-derived taper calendar, attempt selection, scheme selection, weak-point taxonomy, red flags, and communication conventions.

nodes.label: Frozen Engine Numbers
nodes.rationale: The shipped engine numbers are frozen and trusted - acc 4x6 @ 67-75 linear, trans 4x4 @ 77-86 linear, realization 87-93 singles/doubles, deload 62%, meet week 60/55, RTS RPE table, attempts 91/97/101.5, last heavy DL 10-14 d, openers 7-10 d. Advise around them, never contradict silently; factory golden tests must stay byte-identical; new schemes are opt-in equal citizens, never upgrades.

nodes.label: Long-Term Delayed Training Effect (LTDE)
nodes.rationale: Verkhoshansky's causal model behind block periodization: concentrated loading depresses performance on purpose and fitness expresses only after load is removed. Accumulation fatigue is the intended state; the taper unmasks fitness rather than adding it - hence cut volume first, intensity last.

nodes.label: RTS/Tuchscherer RPE Table
nodes.rationale: Reps-x-RPE to %1RM grid (e.g. 4 @ 8 = 83.7) used for e1RM (load / table%) judged block-over-block, and for calibrating every scheme's RPE caps against its % bands. Professional default is the hybrid % band with RPE cap - exactly what PeakWeek prescribes.

nodes.label: Flexible Day-One Anchoring
nodes.rationale: Weeks are half-open 7-day calendar intervals from a coach-chosen programDayOne persisted as yyyy-MM-dd plus named timezone (never epoch, never weekOfYear); positional day slots replace Mon-Sun names. Meet alignment strategies A/B/C keep the invariant that the last ~14 days are laid out backward from meetDate with slack pushed to the front; delivery is a reconciliation-based ledger with dedupe keys, not timers.

nodes.label: Attempt Selection Doctrine
nodes.rationale: Engine standard 91/97/101.5 is near-optimal against IPF data (successful thirds preceded by openers at 91% and seconds at 96% of the third), slightly conservative on the opener in the correct direction. Opener = triple-on-a-bad-day; never a PR second; 9/9 beats a bigger 6/9 (winners average 8.46/9); precompute 3 variants per lift for the ~1-minute submission window; bomb-out guard flags openers above ~95% of the last confirmed single.

nodes.label: Scheme Selection Doctrine
nodes.rationale: Because linear ~ undulating meta-analytically, schemes are fit-to-lifter tools: linear for novices, close meets, dishonest-RPE lifters, and auditability; wave for week-5-6 linear collapse, stale 1RMs, variable readiness; DUP for trained lifters, bench-centric goals, boredom; hypertrophy off-season when no meet is on the calendar.

nodes.label: Weak-Point to Exercise Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Failure-point -> fix/builder mapping per lift with engine load modifiers (pause squat 0.90, close-grip 0.92, RDL 0.75, block pull 1.05, etc). Diagnose from 0.5x video, not where the bar stopped; variation work belongs in acc/trans and the last 3-6 weeks are comp-specific; modifiers are starting estimates and variation-to-comp e1RM drift is itself diagnostic.

nodes.label: Programming Red Flags
nodes.rationale: Thirteen coach-facing catches: junk volume, fatigue masking, proportional/missing taper, adjacent or pre-taper deloads, taper cut >70% or cessation >7 d, heavy pulls inside 7 days, unvalidated attempts, specificity inversion, no volume progression, novice RPE-driven loading, stacking missed sessions, bodyweight drift near the class limit, and block-over-block e1RM decline.

nodes.label: Conjugate Pool Additions
nodes.rationale: Six Westside-style exercises staged for the seed pools ahead of the full conjugate build: floor press 0.92, low pin press 0.94, high pin press 1.05, knee-height block pull 1.05, halting deadlift 0.88, and good morning kept RPE-only because it is too form-sensitive for tight percentages.

nodes.label: Composability Principle (Per-Phase Schemes)
nodes.author: Rick
nodes.rationale: Rick (2026-08-03): we can always find interesting ways to combine training techniques, or use different techniques for different phases, if that is what works for the client. Therefore build per-phase schemes, not monolithic program types: each BlockPlan phase carries its own template set and progression scheme (e.g. DUP accumulation -> wave transmutation -> standard realization); conjugate and hypertrophy presets are internally just phase+scheme combinations, so everything mixes. Sequencing: wave -> DUP -> hypertrophy off-season -> conjugate.

nodes.label: Conjugate (Westside) Roadmap Item
nodes.rationale: The biggest build, sequenced last: ME/DE week shape with rotating variations needs an exercise-rotation policy over the UUID library pools, a new work-up-to prescription style (additive optional Slot field keeps it decode-safe), and DE wave percentages (50-55-60 plus accommodating-resistance note).

nodes.label: Pull/Push Balance Fixes
nodes.rationale: The 20-agent audit found DUP 5-day running 21 pressing vs 9 pulling sets (~2.3:1) against the coach's balanced pull/push priority, with 9 back sets below the ~10-set priority-group floor. Fixes mirror the factory 5-day pattern (swap DB Shoulder Press for Pull-Up, reorder Lat Pulldown before isolation) and touch accessories only - main-lift numbers are frozen.

nodes.label: Round 2 Coach Decisions
nodes.author: Rick
nodes.rationale: Coach-applied on 2026-08-03: new CORE pool on squat days (phase-tapered, none in realization/meet); biceps in off-season only, with curls replacing the third triceps slot (fatigue-aware call keeping meet prep curl-free); Barbell Row 3x10 -> 4x10 for a 10-set weekly back floor; and RIR rendering for ALL accessories in texts, PDFs (EFFORT column), and the editor while percentage work keeps RPE.

nodes.label: PeakWeekClient iOS App Target
nodes.rationale: iOS 16.0 application target (iPhone-only, Swift 5.9, automatic signing, marketing version 0.1.0) displaying as PeakWeek; sources in PeakWeekClient/ with a generated Info.plist.

nodes.label: PeakWeekCore Swift Package
nodes.rationale: Local Swift package at path .. (the repo root) whose PeakWeekCore product the iOS client links - the shared core containing the engine.

nodes.label: X-PW-Token Auth Scheme
nodes.rationale: RLS is enabled with ZERO policies - service-role only - so the anon key merely satisfies the function gateway. Real credentials travel in X-PW-Token: SHA-256-hashed device tokens for phones and a coach token for the Mac stored 0600 at ~/Library/Application Support/PeakWeek/sync-token, with a documented rotation procedure.

nodes.label: lemon-tree Supabase Project
nodes.rationale: The backend lives fully namespaced (pw_* tables, peakweek-videos bucket, peakweek-api function) inside the existing project lemon-tree (zfelhehlwglvakpaelrj) to avoid a $10/mo dedicated project; the migration path to a dedicated project is: apply migrations, redeploy functions, re-mint the coach token, update SyncService.baseURL/anonKey - nothing else changes.

nodes.label: Sample Week-1 Coaching PDF (Sarah Martinez)
nodes.rationale: Week 1 of 12 accumulation deliverable (Aug 10-16, 11 wks out): factory 4-day template with computed loads (Comp Squat 4x6 @ 67% = 210 lb), RIR in the EFFORT column for accessories, coach notes, and the standing RPE guide footer.

nodes.label: Sample Meet-Week Coaching PDF (Sarah Martinez)
nodes.rationale: Week 12 of 12 meet-week deliverable: Mon/Tue technique primer at 60/55%, Wed-Fri rest, and a meet-day attempt table at ~91/~97/~101.5% with the opener-equals-worst-day-triple rule printed for the athlete.
